name: Mnemovast
description: Mnemovast accelerates the hippocampal consolidation process, converting short-term working memory into durable long-term storage at roughly four times the natural rate. Taken after intensive study or information absorption, it chemically enforces synaptic long-term potentiation during sleep, ensuring near-perfect retention of whatever was processed in the preceding 4-6 hours. Standard issue for certification academies and corporate training programs.
effects: Near-perfect retention of pre-dose learning period
Reduced memory decay curve over weeks
side_effects: Hypervivid, sometimes disturbing dreams — consolidation bleeds into REM content
Occasional false memory formation if emotional state was high during encoding
Long-term overuse: difficulty forgetting — traumatic or unwanted memories also locked permanently
Interference with natural memory pruning leading to cognitive clutter
duration: Active during 6-8 hour sleep window following dose
cultural_context: Mnemovast is the student drug of GLMZ, taken before sleep the night before examinations or certification assessments. Novafold markets it aggressively to academies and corporate training centers. The 'Stone' street name reflects both its consolidating effect and a grimmer truth — long-term users report being unable to let go of anything, carrying every bad memory with the same crystal clarity as their professional knowledge. Grief counselors have documented a surge in treatment-resistant trauma disorders among heavy users.
story_hooks: A corporate trainer has been dosing employees with Mnemovast without their knowledge, added to the water supply of a company retreat facility — the retention numbers are extraordinary, but one employee is now haunted by a traumatic incident she witnessed during the training weekend and cannot stop reliving it.

A Tier 2 student used Mnemovast obsessively through her entire academic career and passed every certification — but she also remembers every cruelty, every humiliation, every loss in perfect detail and is quietly unraveling.
A batch of Mnemovast has been contaminated with a foreign-memory compound — users are consolidating not just their own experiences but fragmentary implanted memories of unknown origin.
